failure_annotations.explanation: The orange object remains between the fingers as the arm moves relative to the stationary bowls (right, frames 700–750); left confirms it being carried at frames 760–785. The robot then lowers and releases this unrelated object into the turquoise bowl (left and right, frames 800–879), rather than stacking bowls. This supports wrong-object handling, not a physical grasp failure. The interaction is already underway at the window start and may extend into earlier unseen execution; unlike the preceding prediction's collision-only interpretation, this window establishes controlled transport and placement. Withdrawal begins around frame 880, followed by bowl-directed handling.
failure_annotations.recovery: Remove the orange object from the bowl and set it safely on a clear tabletop area, then grasp a bowl rim and align the bowls for stacking; no human intervention is visibly required.
failure_annotations.severity_evidence: An unrelated object is relocated into a bowl, but no breakage, spill or meaningful damage risk is visible.
failure_annotations.resetability_evidence: Returning to the prior clear-bowl state requires a straightforward removal of the orange object; both bowls and the object remain accessible, so this can be done by the robot without a required human reset.
